lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Five poems mourn the desolation of Jerusalem, confess that the LORD afflicted her for her transgressions, and in the middle chapter turn to hope in the LORD's mercies, ending with a prayer for restoration.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Lamentations mourns and which verses in chapter 3 express hope?
ev: Say what the five chapters of Lamentations are about
Name the hopeful turning point in the book (3:21-26)

nodes.d: Jerusalem is pictured as a widow weeping with none to comfort her; her adversaries prevail because of her many transgressions, and she cries to the LORD, confessing that he is righteous.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Lamentations 1 pictures Jerusalem and what she confesses?
ev: Describe how the city is pictured in Lamentations 1:1-2
Say why the LORD has afflicted her (1:5, 8)
Quote the confession in 1:18

nodes.t: The LORD has done what he planned
nodes.d: The poet describes the LORD acting like an enemy in anger, overthrowing the stronghold, altar and sanctuary, with children dying in the streets; the prophets failed to reveal the iniquity, and the people are urged to pour out their hearts to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Lamentations 2 describes the LORD's anger and what the people are urged to do?
ev: Describe what the LORD has done to Zion (2:1-8)
Say what is said of the prophets (2:14)
Describe the call to pray in 2:18-19

nodes.t: I am the man who has seen affliction
nodes.d: The speaker describes his affliction under the rod of the LORD's wrath as darkness, walls and arrows, remembering the wormwood and the gall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the images the speaker uses for his affliction in Lamentations 3:1-18?
ev: List the images of affliction used in Lamentations 3:1-18
Quote the speaker's state of mind in 3:18-20

nodes.d: In the middle of suffering the speaker recalls that the LORD's mercies never fail, are new every morning, and that it is good to wait for him, because he will not cast off for ever and does not afflict willingly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} quote Lamentations 3:22-23 and say why the speaker has hope?
ev: Quote Lamentations 3:22-23
Explain what he says to do in 3:25-30
Say what 3:31-33 says about the LORD's compassion

nodes.t: Let us search our ways and turn again
nodes.d: The people call each other to examine their ways and return to the LORD, confess rebellion, and the speaker recalls calling from the dungeon, being heard, and asks the LORD to judge his enemies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the call to search our ways in Lamentations 3:40 and what the speaker recalls about calling on the LORD?
ev: Quote the call in Lamentations 3:40-41
Describe the speaker's deliverance in 3:55-58
Describe his prayer against enemies (3:64-66)

nodes.t: The gold grown dim: famine and the sins of priests and prophets
nodes.d: The sanctuary stones lie in the streets, children starve, the sins of prophets and priests who shed blood are named as the cause, and Edom is told its cup is coming while Zion's punishment is accomplished.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Lamentations 4 says caused the city's suffering and what it says at the end about Edom and Zion?
ev: Describe the famine (4:3-10)
Say who is blamed (4:13)
Say what is said of Edom and of Zion (4:21-22)

nodes.t: Remember, O LORD, what is come upon us
nodes.d: The people ask the LORD to remember their reproach and the loss of everything, acknowledge that the crown has fallen because they sinned, affirm his throne is for ever, and pray that he turn them and renew their days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the people ask in Lamentations 5:19-22 and what they confess about themselves?
ev: List what the people have lost (5:2-14)
Quote the confession and the prayer (5:16, 19-21)

nodes.t: The fall of Jerusalem and the exiles recounted
nodes.d: The book closes with Zedekiah's rebellion, the siege, the burning of the temple, the stripping of the bronze pillars and vessels, the executions at Riblah, the numbers carried to Babylon, and Jehoiachin's release and honour in Babylon.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the fall of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 52 and how the chapter ends with Jehoiachin?
ev: Retell the fall of Jerusalem (52:4-14)
Say what is taken from the temple (52:17-23)
Describe what happens to Jehoiachin (52:31-34)
